title: Sean Connery quit playing James Bond. His kid brother took over

 Credit: Dangerous Minds / United Artists / Titanus Movies Sean Connery quit playing James Bond. His kid brother took over
 Will Howard Mon 16 November 2026 13:19, UK Before he became James Bond , one wonders whether for a period of time, Sean Connery was considered the shame of the family. 
 After all, his family were a fairly working-class bunch from Fountainbridge, Edinburgh. He was the son of a cleaner and a lorry driver who did pretty well for themselves, raising two sons and seemingly setting them up for a similar life of honest work and steady pay. The kind of thing that in 2026 seems like a distant fantasy. Then, the strangest thing happened. Sean decided that life wasn’t for him and that he was instead destined for the stage and the screen. 
 Which proceeded to go really, really badly. Yeah, while people talk about James Bond needing to be played by an unknown, Connery would have given his chest hair for a career like Jack Lowden or Callum Turner before he took the role of the iconic superspy. He talked about how for ten whole years his career consisted of background roles in films, bit parts on TV and minor roles on stage, which barely scraped him a living while his younger brother Neil knuckled down and got to work as a plasterer. 
 For a long time, Neil really would have seemed like the success of the family. Until suddenly, he wasn’t. His brother was now one of the world’s biggest celebrities . The only reason anyone who didn’t know him talked about Neil Connery was to marvel that James Bond’s brother was a “mere” plasterer. At least until he lost his job. Then the story was that James Bond’s brother had lost his job as a plasterer for misplacing his tools. Ouch. 
 However, this was 1967, after Connery senior had done five James Bond pictures in five years. Understandably enough, he was done with the intense schedule and decided to leave the role. So I guess both brothers were technically out of a job at the same time. Maybe they could relate to each other that way? The clout that Neil’s second name gave him meant that he could take his case for unfair dismissal public, being interviewed on the radio about it by a rep from his trade union. 
 Which was when Terence Young, director of three of Sean’s Bond films, found out the damnedest thing. You see, the Bond films had been so phenomenally popular that an industry of low-budget spy flicks had sprung up to try and cash in on them . Most of them were spoof comedies and most of them were godawful, but Young knew that they made money, so they’d be in production. Now, they could have a Sean Connery of their own. Not because Sean would look twice at an offer they could make, even if they could afford him. 
 But because it turns out the Connery drawl runs in the family. Neil was the vocal spit of his brother. And now he was looking for work. 
 Young told Italian director Dario Sabatello all this, and he was on the next flight to Edinburgh before the conversation was over. Neil hadn’t thought about acting, but the pay was good, and it seemed like a laugh, so  he took the role in a film that received a slightly bizarre title built from the way the Italian crew kept addressing Neil during his screentest. “OK Connery, OK”. Thus, production began on O.K Connery , a film which Sabatello apparently offered Sean a small part in as well. It seems a little surprising that Sabatello escaped with his life. 
 The film, titled Operation Kid Brother in the United States, was godawful. Neil Connery had all the acting skills of a man who’d spent a decade and change working as a plasterer, and after getting the role because he sounded like his older brother, he ended up being dubbed in the end. This was standard procedure for low-budget pictures of the time, and he was originally going to dub himself, then got appendicitis right around the time of post-production. 
 Either the film’s budget didn’t extend to rebooking the studio time or the director decided to just cut their losses on a film star that couldn’t act, so they drafted in another actor to dub his lines. The cherry on top of it all? The actor was American, and dubbed Neil’s lines in his natural American accent. Not even bothering to put on a comedy Sean Connery impression that even then would have come naturally to 85% of the known world. 
 Even outside of its star, the half-baked spy hokum they crafted for him doesn’t even really work as an intentional comedy. As an unintentional comedy though? There are few more fun times to be had with mates and beers on a bad movie night . Maybe stick to the  Mystery Science Theatre 3000  version of the film, but either way, all connoisseurs of terrible movies should give this absolute stunner of a picture a try.
